Beginning in 776 BC, the Olympic Games were held in the Valley of Olympia in Greece.

In time boxing, a chariot race, and other events were included.
Women were not allowed to attend the games.
The victors of these early games were awarded with wreaths from an olive tree that was planted by Hercules, founder of the Games.
The Olympic Games were abolished in 394 AD.
